title: rbac-patterns-for-privacy-zones-2026
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary

This document defines recommended implementation patterns for role-based access control (RBAC) when applied to privacy zones and sensitive data scopes across Redwood Inference. It ties RBAC constructs to audit logging, data residency and retention requirements, secure SDLC checkpoints, incident response wiring, and the evidence packaging needed for compliance reviews.

Purpose

Provide pragmatic, repeatable patterns teams can adopt to ensure consistent authorization, auditability, and retention behavior when services operate on sensitive or residency-bound datasets. This is intended for platform engineers, product security reviewers, and SREs implementing access controls on Redwood systems (hosted API, Dedicated, Private).

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood services that process customer inference inputs/outputs, model artifacts, or tenant metadata.
- Includes service-to-service identities, human operator roles, CI/CD pipelines, and third-party connectors.
- Does not replace regulatory legal guidance; treat this as engineering guidance aligned to internal compliance controls.

Principles

- Least privilege by default: grant the narrowest role with explicit allowed actions.
- Zone-first design: classify resources into privacy zones and apply role templates per zone.
- Audit-first operations: every authorization decision must produce a structured audit event that is retained according to the zone policy.
- Evidenceable changes: role changes and entitlement assignments must be traceable to a ticket or approval artifact.

Definitions

- Privacy zone: a named classification for data residency or sensitivity (e.g., global-general, eu-personal, regulated-hipaa, pii-high).
- Role template: a reusable RBAC role with parameterized scopes and constraints (e.g., read-only-logs, model-deploy, kv-ops).
- Entitlement store: centralized service storing role assignments, change history and proofs (service name: entitlement-store).
- AuthZ service: central policy decision point (service name: authz-service) that evaluates requests and emits audit events to audit-stream.

Zone matrix (example)

| Zone | Description | Default log retention | Owner |
|------|-------------|------------------------|-------|
| global-general | Non-sensitive telemetry and public config | 90 days | infra-sec |
| eu-personal | EU customer data requiring GDPR mapping | 3 years (access logs) | data-governance |
| regulated-hipaa | PHI-related inference data in private deployments | 7 years | compliance |
| pii-high | High-risk PII (SSNs, financial identifiers) | 10 years (audit trace) | security |

Note: retention periods above are baseline engineering defaults. Legal/regulatory teams may require longer retention or special handling for legal holds.

Role templates and attribute patterns

Adopt a small set of role templates and combine them with resource attributes to reduce role explosion. Example templates:

- admin-lite: cluster-level read/write for non-PII operational tasks.
- deployer: can create model-serving deployments within permitted zones.
- log-reader: read-only access to decrypted logs for a defined timeframe.
- vault-key-operator: manage KMS keys for tenant-scope crypto material.

Attribute-driven scoping (ABAC hybrid):

- resource.zone = <privacy-zone>
- resource.sensitivity = {low, medium, high} 
- subject.team = <team-id>
- request.purpose = {support, dev, incident-response} (must be provided for human-initiated privileged actions)

Pattern: allow role template + attribute constraints. For example, the deployer role is only actionable if resource.zone != regulated-hipaa OR subject has documented HIPAA training attribute.

Implementation checklist (step-by-step)

1. Classify resources: run a discovery job to tag data stores and APIs with resource.zone and resource.sensitivity.
2. Populate role templates: add the canonical templates to entitlement-store and document intended constraints.
3. Integrate policy evaluation: ensure services call authz-service for every sensitive operation and attach the returned decision id to request metadata.
4. Emit structured audit event: authz-service should emit an event with {decision_id, subject, role, resource_id, zone, timestamp, reason} to audit-stream.
5. Retention mapping: map audit-stream topics to retention S3 buckets or cold storage based on zone.
6. Approval evidence: when granting elevated entitlements, require a ticket ID and store the approval artifact link in entitlement-store.

Audit logging and retention mapping

Rules:

- All authz decisions for zone != global-general must be logged as structured JSON.
- Audit events must be shipped to audit-stream within 2s of decision (p99 <= 2s).
- Audit ingestion SLO: 99.9% of events ingested within 30s.

Example audit event schema (abbreviated):

{
  "decision_id": "d-1234abcd",
  "subject": "svc:inference-gateway",
  "action": "model.invoke",
  "resource_id": "tenant-987/model-v3",
  "zone": "eu-personal",
  "outcome": "allow",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-22T15:42:07Z"
}

Data residency and storage controls

- Storage buckets containing sensitive logs for eu-personal or regulated-hipaa must be tagged with region and residency policy and placed in the matching cloud partition.
- Cross-border transfer must be represented as a separate audit event and flagged for legal review.

Table: storage mapping

| Zone | Storage class | Retention policy | Encryption | Example bucket prefix |
|------|---------------|------------------|------------|-----------------------|
| eu-personal | s3-standard (eu) | 3y | KMS-origin-key | eu-audit/tenant/ |
| regulated-hipaa | s3-glacier-vault | 7y | HSM-wrapped | hipaa-archive/ |
| pii-high | s3-standard-ia | 10y | KMS-cmk | pii-archive/ |

Secure SDLC checkpoints (how RBAC changes are gated)

- Design review: any proposal that changes role semantics or template behavior requires a security design review ticket.
- Code gates: authz-service and entitlement-store changes must pass unit tests, policy regression tests, and a staging integration test that validates audit emission and retention mapping.
- Deploy gates: role template changes are staged to a canary namespace and monitored for 48 hours for unexpected denies/errors before organization-wide rollout.

Incident response wiring

- Authorization anomalies (e.g., sudden spike in denies or successful privilege escalation) must trigger an alert to the security on-call.
- Incident playbooks should include steps to:
  1. Freeze entitlement assignments in entitlement-store (read-only mode).
  2. Extract decision_ids for the timeframe and run an automated correlation to identify affected resources and subjects.
  3. Initiate legal hold on related buckets and extend retention as needed.

Example incident run steps (numbered):

1. Triage: Run the authz anomaly query for the last 24 hours using the decision_id index.
2. Containment: Add a temporary global deny rule in authz-service for the affected role-template.
3. Forensics: Export audit events to forensic-store (immutable) and attach the ticket.
4. Remediation: Rollback the offending change via entitlement-store history and publish the post-incident summary.

Compliance evidence packaging (how to assemble artifacts)

Required artifacts per elevated entitlement change:

- Role change diff from the entitlement-store (exportable CSV).
- Approval artifact link (ticket/PR).
- Related audit events (decision_id range) and ingestion proof (S3 manifest).
- Post-deployment verification runbook outputs.

Packaging steps (ordered):

1. Export role-change and approval artifacts.
2. Export decision_ids and corresponding audit JSONs from audit-stream for the change window.
3. Create an evidence bundle in the compliance bucket and record a checksum manifest.
4. Assign evidence owner and retention label (legal_hold/no_hold).

Example RBAC policy snippet (declarative JSON)

{
  "role_template": "deployer",
  "constraints": {
    "allowed_zones": ["global-general", "eu-personal"],
    "requires_training": true
  }
}

Ownership and rollout plan

- Owner: security (primary), infra (secondary) — contact: security-oncall@redwood.com
- Rollout phases:
  - Phase 1: discovery and tagging (2 weeks)
  - Phase 2: entitlement-store role template publishing (1 week)
  - Phase 3: authz-service integration and audit-stream verification (2 weeks)
  - Phase 4: staged rollout and monitoring (4 weeks)

Metrics to monitor

- authz-decision-rate p95/p99 latency (goal: p95 <= 10ms, p99 <= 75ms)
- audit-ingest-latency p99 <= 30s
- unexpected-deny-rate (target < 0.1% of requests for non-sensitive zones)

Related resources

- RBAC policy reference: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/rbac-policy-cookbook-2025
- Entitlement store API: internal://entitlement-store/docs
- Audit schema registry: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-schema-versioning-and-evidence-tagging-2026

Appendix: quick CLI snippets

- Export role template:

  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
    https://entitlement-store.internal/api/v1/role-templates/deployer | jq . > deployer-template.json

- Query recent decisions for a subject:

  curl -s -G https://audit-query.internal/api/decisions --data-urlencode "subject=svc:inference-gateway" --data-urlencode "since=2026-09-01T00:00:00Z" | jq .
